conflict_topics: ventilation / closing service yard door and opening window
laundry absorption of smell / laundry schedule
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants used practical, specific proposals (time windows, ventilation steps, laundry days) rather than abstract complaints, which supported resolution.
Some duplicate lines appear (Agent D's acceptance duplicated and Agent C's confirmations repeated), creating mild repetition.
Speakers consistently referenced the shared physical facts (kitchen, service yard, laundry), keeping the discussion grounded.
evaluation.final_reason: Parties reached a package of adjustments: Agent D agreed to cook after 7 (Agent D: "Okay, after 7 is fine. I can do that."), to notify before starting and to open the kitchen window and close the service-yard door when cooking (Agent D: "Okay, I can do that. Open the window, close the yard door, and I'll let you know before I start."; Agent B requested this: "Just let me know before you start so I can close my door."), and to avoid cooking on the days when Agent C routinely leaves laundry in the yard (Agent C: "I do my laundry on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. If you cook it on the other days, the laundry won't be there."; Agent D: "Okay. Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays, or Sundays. That works for me."). A accepted the time compromise (after 7). B agreed to the notify-and-close-door arrangement. C adjusted by stating her laundry schedule and accepted the days D proposed. These mutually accepted, concrete concessions resolved the substantive incompatibilities.
position_change_notes: Agent D softened original position: initially defended cooking as culturally important (R2) but accepted time limits and scheduling (R3: "Okay, after 7 is fine..."; R9: agreed to specific days).
Agent A softened from 'nobody cook strong-smelling food' (opening) to a time-based compromise (R3: proposed after 7 / Saturday).
Agent B proposed a ventilation/notification procedure (R6) and accepted D's agreement to it.
Agent C retained concern about laundry absorption but provided a scheduling solution (R8) and later confirmed it worked (R10).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: "The smell stays in the living room for hours. I work here at this table, so it's a problem when I have calls." Agent B: "My room is next to the kitchen. The smell gets in and stays in my clothes." (A's earlier request not answered yet; a substantive grievance/demand is in play.)

Agent C: "Same for my laundry. It's hanging right next to the kitchen." Agent D: "I get it, the smell is strong. But that's the food I grew up with. It's what I cook." (D pushes back by defending continued cooking; clear incompatible interests appear.)

Agent A proposes a time compromise: "Could you cook it after 7, or maybe on a Saturday?" Agent D: "Okay, after 7 is fine. I can do that." (D accepts a proposed constraint, reducing immediate confrontation though not all voices have weighed in.)
Agent B objects to the after-7 arrangement: "That doesn't really fix it for me. The smell will still be there all night." (A–D agreement is contested by B, reopening the dispute.)

Agent C supports B: "Yeah, that doesn't work for my laundry either. It'll just take in the smell all night." Agent D responds constructively: "Okay, then what works for the laundry and the rooms?" (Conflict remains but parties move toward problem-solving.)

Agent B suggests ventilation + notice: "If you open the kitchen window and close the door to the service yard, that might work. Just let me know before you start so I can close my door." Agent D: "Okay, I can do that. Open the window, close the yard door, and I'll let you know before I start." (A practical mitigation accepted for B.)
Agent C: "Closing the door to the yard doesn't help me. My laundry is still in there." (The ventilation/door solution is insufficient for C; the issue is reopened.)

Agent D: "Okay. So what do we do about the laundry?" Agent C proposes a laundry schedule: "I do my laundry on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. If you cook it on the other days, the laundry won't be there." (A concrete scheduling proposal that reduces the incompatibility.)

Agent D accepts the schedule: "Okay. Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays, or Sundays. That works for me." (D affirms the proposed cooking days; combined with earlier acceptance of after-7 and ventilation/notice, the substantive conflicts are addressed.)
Agent C: "Okay, thanks. That works." (Confirmatory acknowledgment; no new substantive disagreement.)

substantive_insights: Conflict balanced competing interests: A's work calls (timing sensitivity) vs D's cultural food preferences (habit/identity).
Ventilation alone didn't solve the problem for everyone; scheduling (who is present/where laundry is hung) mattered as much as air flow.
A multi-part compromise (time limit, ventilation procedure, and laundry-aware days) was required to satisfy all participants.
